title: Atmospheric entry
target: Use energy and geometry to discuss entry heating without claiming a guaranteed outcome.
criteria: Compare kinetic energy with a stated heating requirement.
Explain the role of surface area relative to mass.
Name missing factors in a survival prediction.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: An entry model assigns 150 J of kinetic energy to an object. A specified heating change needs 30 J. What is the energy ratio KE/heating requirement?
cpa.guide: 150/30 = 5. The ratio alone does not specify how much energy heats the object.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An object has 240 J of kinetic energy, but a model sends only 10% into its heating. A specified change needs 40 J. Is the assigned heating energy enough?
options: No; kinetic energy cannot transfer into internal energy.
Yes; 10% means multiply by 10.
No; 24 J is less than 40 J.
Yes; all 240 J must heat the object.
cpa.guide: Apply the stated fraction before comparing: 0.10 × 240 = 24 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Equal-density spheres have radii r and 3r. Area scales as r² and mass as r³. How does area per mass compare for the larger sphere?
options: It is one-third as large.
It is three times as large.
It is nine times as large.
It is unchanged.
cpa.guide: Area grows by 9 and mass by 27; their ratio changes by 9/27 = 1/3.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two equal-density rocks have the same shape but different sizes. Why can the smaller one respond differently to surface heating?
options: Its temperature must always be zero.
It has less area per unit mass.
All sizes have identical area-to-mass ratio.
It has more surface area per unit mass.
cpa.guide: For similarly shaped equal-density bodies, area/mass scales inversely with size.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A calculation shows enough total kinetic energy to melt a rock. What is still needed before claiming it will melt during entry?
options: Energy-transfer fraction, duration, material behavior, and losses.
No further information; all kinetic energy always heats the rock.
Only the rock’s name.
Only the total kinetic energy again.
cpa.guide: Available energy is not identical to absorbed energy or a complete thermal history.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A simplified entry model omits fragmentation and changing shape. Which statement is appropriate?
options: A conditional model cannot be useful for any comparison.
The omitted processes cannot matter by definition.
The model proves exact impact damage.
Its survival estimate is conditional because fragmentation can change area, mass, and heating.
cpa.guide: Changing geometry and mass can affect drag and heat transfer; state those limitations.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
